subject: RFI: Support & TAM coverage – Oceanview Financial
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@oceanview.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Havers <thavers@oceanview.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Support & TAM coverage – Oceanview Financial

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for agreeing to take our RFI on support coverage and TAM engagement details. To help our procurement and security teams evaluate vendors, can you provide a short-form response that covers the items below? Ideally we get a draft by EOD Friday (Oct 2).

Required sections:
- TAM hours / coverage model (on-call? coverage per account size; US/EU hours)
- Escalation path and SLA targets (P1/P2/P3 response and remediation targets; when do engineering escalations occur)
- Incident communication cadence and templates (initial ack, incident updates, post-incident report timing)
- Staff security screening and background checks for on-site TAMs (if applicable)
- Contact stringency and role matrix (who is primary, backup, exec escalation)

If you can attach a simple matrix or workbook that maps account tiers to TAM rotation and SLA targets, that would be very helpful. Please also include any sample incident communication templates.

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Sr. Procurement Manager | Oceanview Financial
elena.ruiz@oceanview.com
Attachments: none

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@oceanview.com>
Cc: Tom Havers <thavers@oceanview.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 14:03:21 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Support & TAM coverage – Oceanview Financial

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Attached is a first-pass workbook (redwood-tam-coverage-matrix.xlsx) and an incident comms sample (incident-communication-sample.docx). The workbook maps three account tiers (Starter / Production / Mission-Critical) to TAM coverage, on-call schedules, and SLA targets.

A few clarifying notes inline below:
- TAM hours: our baseline is 9x5 business-hours coverage for Starter, 24x5 for Production, and 24x7 for Mission-Critical (with follow-the-sun coverage for US/EU/APAC). For this RFI I included the US baseline; we can add explicit EU timezone shifts if you want.
- Escalation: P1 incidents trigger on-call TAM -> Escalation Engineer -> Incident Commander (platform ops). P1 target: initial ack within 15 minutes, mitigation plan within 1 hour, and continuous updates every 30 minutes until mitigation. P2: ack within 1 hour, next update within 4 hours.
- Incident comms: attached doc contains an initial ack template and 1/4/12/24-hour update cadence examples. We send a PIR within 72 hours for most P1 events and a written RCA within 7 business days when full analysis is required.
- Staff screening: all customer-facing TAMs undergo background checks and are bound by our security policies and NDA; for on-prem or on-site roles we can provide additional vetting on request.

Open questions for your team (please confirm):
1) Do you require named (dedicated) TAMs for Mission-Critical accounts or is a shared pool acceptable?
2) Any minimum SLA targets you need us to commit to beyond the targets above?

Next steps: Marissa and Karthik are looped to finalize the matrix and confirm operational details; I plan to send a polished version by end of day Friday.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Manager, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0164
Attachments: redwood-tam-coverage-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB); incident-communication-sample.docx (DOCX, 22KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 10:22:10 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Support & TAM coverage – Oceanview Financial

Jasmine / Karthik —

Quick internal notes while I review the workbook:
- For Mission-Critical accounts that expect a named TAM, we should call out our ramp (30 days) and overlap entitlement (two-week shadowing) in the workbook — customers often ask about transition risk.
- SLA language: recommend we keep the P1 mitigation "plan within 1 hour" but add a caveat for third-party outages (cloud provider) where our mitigation is collaboration and coordination; propose a separate row for joint response scenarios.
- Incident comms: add a short Exec Summary template for customers who require board-level updates (one-paragraph impact + timeline).

I made three cell edits in the matrix (notes column) — nothing major. If Oceanview requires on-site background check proof, we have HR contact info to issue local vendor checks; mark that as "available upon request" to avoid over-sharing initial docs.

Happy to sign-off once Jasmine confirms the named vs shared TAM preference question.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
Attachments: none

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@oceanview.com>, Tom Havers <thavers@oceanview.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 15:45:03 -0700
Subject: Final: RFI — Support & TAM coverage (Oceanview Financial)

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks for the chat earlier this week. Attached is the polished workbook and an updated incident communications sample that includes an executive summary template and the named-TAM ramp details we discussed. Highlights:
- TAM coverage: Starter = 9x5; Production = 24x5 (follow-the-sun fallback); Mission-Critical = 24x7 with optional named TAM. Named TAMs: 30-day ramp + two-week shadowing.
- Escalation & SLAs: P1 ack = 15 min; mitigation plan = 1 hour; update cadence = every 30 min until stabilization. We included a row for joint-response scenarios (third-party/cloud provider).
- Incident comms: Initial ack within 15 minutes, rolling updates at 30/60/180 minutes, PIR within 72 hours and full RCA summary available within 7 business days. Exec summary template included.
- Security & screening: background checks and customer-facing staff vetting are "available upon request"; we can provide HR confirmation letters for on-site assignments.

Files attached: redwood-tam-coverage-matrix.xlsx; incident-communication-sample.docx

Next steps: please confirm whether Oceanview wants dedicated(named) TAMs for the Mission-Critical tier and whether any SLA targets need adjustment. Once you confirm, we will prepare final RFP artifacts and sign the mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Manager, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
